question_text: What is the purpose of the 10th Amendment?

official_answers.text: (It states that the) powers not given to the federal government belong to the states or to the people.

why_it_matters.text: The 10th Amendment makes the basic rule of American government clear: the federal government has only the powers the Constitution gives it — nothing more. Everything else stays with the states, or with the people themselves.

fun_fact.text: The 10th Amendment is the last original amendment from the Bill of Rights — and it's the 'everything else' rule. Anti-Federalists worried the federal government would grab powers not on its list. The 10th flipped the assumption: if a power isn't given to Washington, it belongs to the states or the people.
